angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: how hard a receiver pushes off the ground at the sharpest point of his cut), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner), tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out classes. The positive use is last season's route-shrunk SOE as a day-3 tiebreaker, with break-phase speed traces as a film cue.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = 0.021 g (sd of true receiver Break G).
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [-3.6, +1.0], n=116 on unseen classes (+3 in rejected). Same-route-family noise-corrected correlation 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32], n=99. Day-3 SOE tiebreaker: season-fold rank-correlation gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63] over 20 pairs (one estimand; leave-one-receiver-out 0.63 is now only an appendix sensitivity row). Pre-specified matched contrasts: 62% [41, 80] of 53.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_15/revised per the R15 judges. (1) One number per claim: the day-3 headline is now the season-fold gain 0.31, and leave-one-receiver-out 0.63 sits beside it in an appendix reconciliation table that explains the gap (a negative LORO baseline of -0.43). Noise-corrected 0.02 (n=99) and raw rho -0.11 (n=115) are labelled as two estimands. Price is stated once (9% [2, 17]). The 'earlier rounds' references and the 'Clearer in the larger pool' row are gone. (2) Gibbs/EIV, Platt and the nested test are moved to a short appendix methods paragraph. Added a 'Why now, why receivers' paragraph and a one-sentence Break G definition, with the sd in a footnote. (3) Pre-registration: frozen_rule_2026.json (coefficients, shrinkage, Platt, threshold, 13 names and probabilities, primary/secondary tests) with sha256 and freeze date. Power calculation: about 18 expected pairs, power 0.37 at the observed gain and 0.61 pooled; the hit-rate test needs 9 of 13 (power 0.20). (4) New pre-specified matched-contrast test on all 106 within-season day-3 pairs, with a receiver-clustered bootstrap. Boutte/Washington is relabelled as an illustration chosen for contrast and its verdict softened. (5) Shortlist: act-on names lead (top 4 with 14+ games), availability flag (13 or fewer games), role column (team, alignment, man share, QB), and the rule's earlier lists named with hit/miss. (6) Viz: Fig 1 is a 2x2 layout with league-median reference paths, a shared-axis Break G strip, pooled rho in the banner and a league speed line. Fig 2C greys low-power families, adds a power column and states the price. Fig 3 adds the league IQR band, puts the legend outside and uses larger fonts. Fig 4 drops the all-rounds point, puts check/cross marks in the list columns with 7/13 vs 6/13 headers, enlarges C and adds a 2026-list rug.
open_risks: The day-3 edge is still not proven: the season-fold interval includes 0, and the matched-contrast edge over pick and routes is small (62% vs 59%).
The pre-registration is frozen mid-season (24 October 2026), not before the 2026 season; the 2026 test is underpowered (0.37).
The family model is a bounded null: every slice has power under about 1/3 to detect a true link of 0.2.
The film cue rests on six sampled NFL hitches per player, half of the sample chosen for high EPA.
Not a blind test: all three classes were seen during the rounds of development.
